**4 of 4.** Targets `integration/03-audit-chain-seal`.

The CBAM section, and the one line CBAM is allowed to place on a record.

## A deliberate override of the plan

The integration plan puts CBAM under a parent Emissions section at `/emissions/cbam/*` and says explicitly not to build at `/cbam`. **This does the opposite, on the owner's decision.**

The cost is a URL migration if a second emissions module ever arrives. The gain is that the thing users came for is one click away rather than two, and the section reads the way the rest of the product already does.

## Views, not tabs, not sub-pages

CBAM's screens are views of one section, reached by the same quiet `?view=` toggle Records already uses for Trends and Benchmarks. Arbor's design rules forbid tabs, and a toggle keeps one primary action per screen. The nav link stays active across every view and every case page, so no sub-navigation is introduced.

An unknown `?view=` falls back to Cases rather than erroring — a stale or mistyped link is a navigation hint, not an instruction, and should land somewhere useful.

A test asserts Records does **not** activate on `/cbam`: cases, consignments and goods lines live under this section and are not pushed into Arbor's record model.

## The record cross-reference

The single sanctioned exception, and required rather than optional. Without it a user can look at a supplier and not know that supplier carries six figures of exposure — the point at which the case for merging the two products fails.

One line: in-scope status, exposure, link into the section. An entity not in scope gets **no line at all**, because a "not in scope" line on every supplier trains people to skip it on the ones where it matters.

The exposure figure follows the rule set in the fix phase: a number whose inputs are placeholder-derived renders an em-dash and names what is missing. **A zero would read as "no exposure"**, and an unbacked number is worse than a missing one.

## What is not here

The remaining Phase 5 screens — case pages, the field review extension, the CPR check, the supplier request builder — are UI against an API that has never been called for real. `NUCLEOS_URL` does not exist yet; the extraction and calculate endpoints are exercised only by tests.

Building four screens against an unproven boundary means a shape mismatch becomes four screens to rework rather than one client to fix. **Deploying `nucleos/` and pushing one real document through is the next step**, before more UI.
